messages:
alan: FYI during the nightly staging smoke tests a bunch of jobs started failing with Vault decrypt errors for secrets that were previously fine. Error looks like: `vault: transit: bad ciphertext: unsupported key version`.

jo: Oof. Any recent key rotations or rewraps in staging?

rachel: I pushed a rekey to the staging transit key last night to rotate out a compromised key material (per ticket SEC-2026-88). It succeeded but I didn't validate the consumer pipelines.

alan: Looks like some partner connectors are still writing tokens encrypted with the older key version. Vault rejects them now. We need a quick mitigation plan so services don't fail.

priya: Short options: 1) Re-enable the previous key version temporarily (if available) 2) Rewrap existing ciphertexts to the new key version via a one-off job 3) Rollback the rekey (hard). Prefer (1) or (2).

alan: Can we re-enable previous key version? Is that safe from a security perspective?

rachel: GCP KMS allowed disabling a version but we archived it. We can re-enable for a short window. Tradeoff: exposing old key again vs immediate availability. If we re-enable, we must also rotate consumer tokens and add audit logging.

infra-bot: detected: staging-vault-transit-key rekey completed by rachel at 2026-03-22T23:12:09Z (operation id op-77b2).

vault-bot: vault audit: last decrypt attempts failed 153 entries since 2026-03-23T01:00Z.

jo: Technical plan I can run fast: 1) Re-enable previous key version in KMS for 30 minutes. 2) Run `vault transit:rewrap` job to rewrap ciphertexts in staging buckets to new key version. 3) Revoke short-lived tokens that used the old ciphertext and force re-issue. 4) Enable KMS and Vault decrypt audit to our SIEM.

alan: Commands we think will work (jo will run):
```
# re-enable key version
gcloud kms keys versions enable 4 --key=staging-transit-key --keyring=staging-keyring --location=us-central1
# list objects with old ciphertext pattern (quick scan)
gsutil ls gs://staging-secrets/** | xargs -n1 -I {} gsutil cat {} | grep -E "v=4\"|v=3\"" || true
# rewrap helper (pseudo)
python tools/rewrap_ciphertexts.py --source-version 3 --target-version 4 --bucket gs://staging-secrets --dry-run
```

priya: When doing this, lock down RBAC: ensure only the rewrap runner service-account has `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` for the short window. Remove broad bindings first. I'll prepare a temporary IAM binding change.

rachel: I'll hold on approving the rollback. Quick question: Does Vault maintain any metadata tying ciphertext -> key version? We saw `v=3` in some payloads. If so, rewraps should be safe.

vault-bot: vault metadata shows `key_version` label for transit-wrapped payloads when clients used `batch_transit_encrypt`. Not all uploads have it, some are opaque. Use sample scan to decide.

jo: I'll run a sampling job to assess how many objects need rewrap and how many clients will need token rotation. If enormous, we'll re-enable old key for longer and schedule a background rewrap migration.

alan: Incident comms: product ops needs a short blurb to say "staging-deployments experienced secret decrypt failures; engineering is mitigating; no production impact". I'll draft.

priya: Post-mortem action items I'll track:
- enforce pre-rotation compatibility checks (test rewraps)
- add pre-rotation checklist in SEC runbook
- add automated detection: fail after rekey if decrypt error rate > X -> rollback guard
- ensure KMS audit export to SIEM and Vault audit retention 90d

rachel: Also add: require a small integration test in partner connectors that verifies decrypt after rekey in a sandbox.

infra-bot: terraform: changes proposed for temporary IAM binding (PR #4987).

jo: Running sampling now, will report counts in 10m. If < 1000 objects we do immediate rewrap. If > 10k we re-enable prior key and schedule background migration.

alan: Owners: jo -> sampling + rewrap or re-enable, priya -> IAM lockstep + SIEM sink, rachel -> hold rollback and assist with rewrap tool, alan -> comms + incident ticket INC-2026-1291. Check-in in 15.

jo: sampling results: ~420 objects reference old key v=3 and ~12 connectors still emitting v=3 tokens. Proceeding with dry-run rewrap now.

rachel: running rewrap dry-run accepted, no failures. Approving live job.

jo: live rewrap started. ETA ~8m.

vault-bot: rewrap job progress: 30% processed, 0 errors.

jo: rewrap complete, all 420 objects rewrapped and validated. Revoke-and-issue new tokens for the 12 connectors scheduled now.

priya: IAM bindings tightened and removed broad decrypt role. SIEM sink enabled for KMS decrypts.

alan: Great work. Logging everything in INC-2026-1291. Will follow up with a short postmortem and checklist. Closing thread; move to incident channel for async updates.
